Intel is hiring an EDA Tools Software Engineer for its PTD Litho Frame Automation Team in Logic Technology Development. The role defines and validates process design rules and tape-in collaterals, creates and verifies VLSI layouts, supports design and PDK verification flows, and develops CAD tools and collateral for process technology development.

Responsibilities
Verify VLSI layout adherence to complex layout design rules, specifically ownership in Quality Assurance of FRAT designs across all Intel process nodes
Troubleshoot design and PDK(Process Design Kit) verification issues with complex physical design flows, both industry standard and Intel tools and flows
Write/update software code for cell design and testcases, verification and package design content for distribution
CAD design development and support of LTD Tape-in Collateral Library for ALL Intel Process Technology nodes including CR experimental Path Finding projects
Collaborating, directing, extracting, executing designs and constructs that will be used for process implementation, monitoring, improvement and development well ahead of any other team in LTD. This interaction will be with a very diverse team including Litho, Integration, Device, Test Chip, Tape Out, and OPC and RET (Reticle Enhancement Team) experts. These designs will be used during development, refined and then made available for HVM (High Volume Manufacturing)

Required
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, with 6+ months of hands-on experience in the domain and demonstrated skills gained through internships, academic projects, coursework, or hands-on training
Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with no prior professional experience
Coursework and background should include VLSI design or CAD, programming in Python or C++, Semiconductor Device Physics or basic electrical circuit theory, Silicon manufacturing flows
Preferred
Familiarity with semiconductor processing/engineering or computer science (from coursework or internship or work experience)
VLSI Circuit mask design layout and/or verification (from coursework or internship or work experience)
Basic solid-state physics, optics and IC (Integrated Circuit) process flow (from coursework or internship or work experience)
Programming skills in a high-level programming language (from coursework or internship or work experience)
Familiarity with UNIX/Linux platforms (from coursework or internship or work experience)
Experience with Cadence Virtuoso, Klayout, and tools such as Calibre DRV or Calibre
Knowledge of design rule checks (DRC), ICV, or IC Validator software tools
Experience with custom design and verification tools, debugging, and flow development
Strong communication and collaboration skills for cross-functional teamwork
Proactive mindset with a focus on continuous improvement and learning
